statement: In machine learning and statistics, the learning rate (also referred to as gain) is a tuning parameter in an optimization algorithm that determines the step size taken at each iteration while moving along a descent direction (typically determined from the gradient of a loss function) toward a minimum of the loss function, either as a scalar or as a diagonal matrix across parameters.

symbols.meaning: learning rate determining the step size
symbols.dimensions: scalar, or p x p diagonal matrix

symbols.meaning: learning rate at iteration step n
drop rate (interval of iterations between learning rate drops)

properties.property: Trade-off between rate of convergence and overshooting
properties.why: too high a learning rate causes the algorithm to jump over minima, while too low a rate either takes too long to converge or gets stuck in undesirable local minima
when the learning rate and its adjustments differ per parameter, the resulting diagonal matrix can be interpreted as an approximation to the inverse Hessian matrix in Newton's method
the learning rate corresponds to the step length determined by inexact line search in quasi-Newton methods and related optimization algorithms
factors in a decay parameter d to alter the learning rate based on the iteration count to settle learning and prevent oscillations
decreases the learning rate by decay factor d at predefined iteration drop intervals r
factors in decay continuously across iteration steps using a decreasing exponential function

assumptions.assumption: Optimization progresses along a descent direction (typically determined from the gradient of the loss function) toward a loss function minimum.
assumptions.breaks_when: The loss function does not provide a well-defined descent direction, or the objective does not involve minimizing a loss function.

assumptions.assumption: Hyperparameters governing learning rate schedules (e.g., initial learning rate \eta_0, decay d, drop rate r) are suitably tuned for the specific problem and model.
assumptions.breaks_when: Hyperparameters are manually misspecified for the specific problem landscape, causing failure to converge or oscillation.

failure_modes.signature: Optimization jumps over minima or oscillates back and forth across a minimum without settling
failure_modes.cause: Learning rate is set too high

failure_modes.signature: Optimization takes an impractically long time to converge or becomes trapped in an undesirable local minimum
failure_modes.cause: Learning rate is set too low

failure_modes.signature: Optimization trajectory rolls past or over the desired minimum
failure_modes.cause: Momentum hyperparameter is set too high

failure_modes.mode: Failure to escape local bumps via momentum
failure_modes.signature: Optimization fails to accelerate along sustained gradient directions or gets trapped by small bumps
failure_modes.cause: Momentum hyperparameter is set too low to fulfill its purpose
